BOARD OF SUPERVISORS, COUNTY OF SAN MATEO, STATE OF CALIFORNIA
RESOLUTION CALLING AND PROVIDING FOR A SPECIAL ELECTION TO BE
HELD ON NOVEMBER 3, 2026 THROUGHOUT THE COUNTY OF SAN MATEO FOR
THE PURPOSE OF VOTING UPON PROPOSED AMENDMENTS TO THE SAN
MATEO COUNTY CHARTER, PROCLAIMING SAID SPECIAL LOCAL
COUNTYWIDE ELECTION PURSUANT TO ELECTIONS CODE SECTION 12001,
REQUESTING THAT THE ELECTION BE CONSOLIDATED WITH ANY AND ALL
OTHER ELECTIONS TO BE HELD ON NOVEMBER 3, 2026, AND REQUESTING
SERVICES OF THE COUNTY'S CHIEF ELECTIONS OFFICER
RESOLVED, by the Board of Supervisors of the County of San Mateo, State of
California, that:
WHEREAS, the County of San Mateo is one of 15 charter counties in California
and has adopted the San Mateo County Charter ("Charter"), which was originally ratified
by San Mateo County voters in 1932; and
WHEREAS, Charter counties have all the powers that are provided by the
California Constitution or by statute for counties, County charters are required to provide
for an elected sheriff, an elected district attorney, an elected assessor, other officers,
their election or appointment, compensation, terms and removal, and the County may
establish an independent redistricting commission by resolution, ordinance, or charter
amendment (Cal. Const. Art. 11, S 4; Elec. Code S 23001); and
WHEREAS, under California law, a Charter amendment may be proposed by the
Board for approval by the qualified voters of San Mateo County at a special election to
occur on the next established election date (Cal. Const. Art. 11, S 3; Gov. Code, SS
WHEREAS, the Board deems it necessary and essential to submit to the
qualified voters of San Mateo County the question of proposed amendments to the
Charter set forth in Section 2 through 5 of this Resolution (referred to herein individually
as "Measure" and collectively as the "Measures"), at a special election to be held on
November 3, 2026, the next available established election date under the law; and
WHEREAS, pursuant to Government Code Section 23730, the special election
on the Measures must be called by ordinance, and thus the Board, at its regular
meeting on May 19, 2026, introduced an Ordinance calling for and proclaiming a special
election to be held on November 3, 2026 throughout the County of San Mateo for the
purpose of voting upon amendments to the San Mateo County Charter, and waive the
reading of the ordinance in its entirety, regarding: 1) Adding to the Charter Preamble a
policy statement on resilience to extreme weather events; and 2) Adding to the Charter
Preamble a policy statement affirming the County's commitment to the dignity, civil
rights, and equal protection of all County residents; and 3) Amending Section 415 of the
County Charter to extend the period in which the County Board of Supervisors is
required to either call a special election or make an appointment in the event of a
vacancy in an elected office other than the Board of Supervisors from 30 days to 60
days, and to require the Board to conduct at least one public meeting to receive public
comment prior to any appointment; and 4) Amending Section 202 of the County Charter
and adding a new Section 202.1 to the County Charter to require that supervisorial
districts be reapportioned following each federal decennia/ census by an independent
redistricting commission pursuant to applicable provisions of the California Elections
Code, and requesting that the election be consolidated with any and all other elections
to be held on November 3, 2026. ("Ordinance"), which will be adopted by the Board at a
regular meeting with this Resolution.
NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS HEREBY RESOLVED as follows:
Call of the Election and Purpose. An election shall be and is hereby
called and ordered to be held on November 3, 2026 throughout San Mateo County for
the purpose of voting upon the proposed amendments to the Charter as set forth in the
Measures and as provided in the Ordinance, a copy of which is attached hereto as
Attachment A and incorporated in full by this reference.
First Measure. The following Measure containing an amendment to the
Charter shall be submitted to the electorate on November 3, 2026:
a) The form of the ballot question for the Measure as it is to appear on the ballot is
as follows:
COUNTY CHARTER AMENDMENT
Shall the San Mateo County Charter be amended to add a provision to
the Charter Preamble designating long-term resilience to extreme
weather events as a County priority?
YES
NO
b) The Measure, if approved by voters, would amend the Charter Preamble to add a
new paragraph to read as follows:
Preamble.
It shall be the policy of San Mateo County that long-term resilience against
extreme weather events — including fire, flood, wind, rain, heat, drought, and sea
level rise — is a County priority, to be undertaken collaboratively with cities,
district, and other public entities.
Second Measure. The following Measure containing an amendment to
the Charter shall be submitted to the electorate on November 3, 2026:
a) The form of the ballot question for the Measure as it is to appear on the ballot is
as follows:
COUNTY CHARTER AMENDMENT
Shall the San Mateo County Charter be amended to add a provision to
the Charter Preamble affirming the County's commitment to the
dignity, civil rights, and equal protection of all County residents?
YES
NO
b) The Measure, if approved by voters, would amend the Charter Preamble to add a
new paragraph to read as follows:
Preamble.
The County of San Mateo affirms its commitment to the dignity, civil rights, and
equal protection of all County residents in a manner that promotes equity,
fairness, inclusion, belonging, accessibility, and opportunity.
Third Measure. The following Measure containing an amendment to the
Charter shall be submitted to the electorate on November 3, 2026:
a) The form of the ballot question for the Measure as it is to appear on the ballot is
as follows:
COUNTY CHARTER AMENDMENT
Shall the San Mateo County Charter be amended to extend the period
in which the County Board of Supervisors is required to either call a
special election or make an appointment in the event of a vacancy in
an elected office other than the Board of Supervisors from 30 days to
60 days, and to require the Board to conduct at least one public
meeting to receive public comment prior to any appointment?
YES
NO
b) The Measure, if approved by voters, would amend and replace in its entirety the
first paragraph of Section 415 of Article IV of the Charter, to read as follows:
415. Vacancies
The Board of Supervisors shall provide for public notice of vacancies on
boards and commissions and of the method by which citizens may apply
for appointments. If a vacancy occurs in an elective office other than the
Board of Supervisors, the Board shall within 60 days of the effective date
of the vacancy, either make an appointment or order the calling of a
special election to fill the vacancy. In the event that the Board elects to
make an appointment, the Board shall hold at least one noticed, public
meeting for the purpose of receiving public comment regarding the
appointment and qualifications of potential candidates. If the Board does
not make an appointment or call a special election within 60 days, the
county officer responsible for conducting county elections shall
immediately order a special election to be called to fill the vacancy. The
appointee shall hold office for the remainder of the term. For purposes of
this section, the special election may be conducted as an all-mailed ballot
election, at the discretion of the Board or the county officer responsible for
conducting elections, as applicable.
Fourth Measure. The following Measure containing an amendment to the
Charter shall be submitted to the electorate on November 3, 2026:
a) The form of the ballot question for the Measure as it is to appear on the ballot is
as follows:
COUNTY CHARTER AMENDMENT
Shall the San Mateo County Charter be amended to require that
supervisorial districts be reapportioned following each federal
decennial census by an independent redistricting commission
pursuant to applicable provisions of the California Elections Code?
YES
NO
b) The Measure, if approved by voters, would amend and replace in its entirety
Section 202 of Article II of the Charter, to read as follows:
202. Election
Supervisors are elected by district.
Candidates for the office of Supervisor shall be electors in the district
which they seek to represent. If a Supervisor ceases to reside in that
district, the seat becomes vacant.
Except as otherwise provided in this Charter, Supervisors shall be
nominated and elected pursuant to general law for a term of four years.
Supervisors shall not be eligible for election to nor serve more than three
consecutive terms in office.
Further, the Measure, if approved by voters, would add Section 201.1 to Article II
of the Charter to read as follows:
202.1. Independent Redistricting Commission
The five supervisorial districts of the County shall be reapportioned in the
manner specified in general law by an independent redistricting
commission, as defined in and governed by applicable provisions of the
California Elections Code.
Voting Requirements and Effective Date. Each Measure may be voted
on separately without prejudice to the other Measures and each Measure will become
effective only if submitted to the voters at the Countywide special election on November
3, 2026, and only after approval by a majority (i.e., 50% + 1) of the qualified voters
voting in the special election. If a Measure passes, the Charter amendment proposed
by the Measure will take effect as provided for in Government Code Sections 23713 and
Proclamation. Pursuant to Elections Code Section 12001, the Board of
Supervisors hereby proclaims that a special Countywide election will be held on
Tuesday, November 3, 2026, to vote upon the Charter amendments as set forth in the
Measures and as described in the Ordinance.
Consolidation. The special election on the Measures shall
be
consolidated with any and all other elections to be held on November 3, 2026.
Election Services and Procedures.
a) The special election on the Charter amendments set forth in the Measures will be
consolidated with any and all other elections to be held on November 3, 2026.
b) All qualified voters in San Mateo County shall be permitted to vote in the special
election on the Charter amendments set forth in the Measures.
c) Pursuant to Government Code Section 23731, the special election shall be held
and conducted, the returns canvassed, and the result declared in the same
manner as provided by law for general elections.
d) The election will be held on November 3, 2026, from the hour of 7:00 a.m. to the
hour of 8:00 p.m., during which period of time the polls will remain continuously
open. At 8:00 p.m., the polls will be closed, except as provided in section 14401
of the Elections Code.
e) Pursuant to Government Code Section 23731, the Chief Elections Officer shall
prepare and mail to each eligible voter in the County a sample ballot and a
voter's pamphlet containing the complete text of the Measures.
f) The Board of Supervisors hereby permits the County's Chief Elections Officer to
render all services specified by Elections Code Section 10418 relating to the
special election on the Measures, to include the publication of notices of election
and the mailing of the sample ballot. The County will pay for all such services
performed by the County's Chief Elections Officer related to the special election
on the Measures.
g) The Board of Supervisors hereby requests that the County's Chief Elections
Officer, and/or designee(s), take all actions which are necessary or appropriate in
connection with the special election on the Measures, including, but not limited
to, printing and mailing sample ballots, arguments, and applications for absentee
ballots, canvassing election returns, and certifying the results of the election to
the Board of Supervisors. The County Attorney's Office shall prepare the
impartial analysis of the Measures.
h) The Clerk of the Board is hereby authorized and directed to deliver a copy of this
Ordinance to the County's Chief Elections Officer, or other appropriate elections
officials of San Mateo County, no later than 88 days prior to the special election
on the Measures, and to give notice of the special election on the Measures by
causing the County's Registration & Elections Division to publish the text of the
Measures and other items, not later than 15 days before the date of the special
election.
i)
j)
The Chief Elections Officer shall establish election precincts, designate the
polling places, and provide election officers for each precinct at the November 3,
2026 election in accordance with the election laws of the State of California.
The members of the Board of Supervisors are hereby authorized, but not
directed, to prepare and file with the County's Registration & Elections Division, a
ballot argument in favor of the Measures within the time established by County's
Registration & Elections Division.
10. Severability Clause. If any section, subsection, paragraph, sentence,
phrase, clause, or word of this Resolution is for any reason found to be invalid or
unenforceable, such section, subsection, paragraph, sentence, phrase, clause, or word
shall be severed from, and shall not affect the validity of, all remaining portions of this
Resolution which can be given effect without the severed portion.
11. Delegated Authority to County Executive. The County Executive, or
designee(s), is hereby directed to take such other actions and to execute such other
documents as are necessary to carry out the purposes of this Resolution.
